key_insight: Confidently wrong LLMs can draw users toward false beliefs while leaving trust largely unchanged and eroding their ability to distinguish correct from incorrect answers.
engineering_relevance: Learning interfaces should make claim-level reliability visible and support independent verification rather than treating confident delivery or user trust as evidence of accuracy.
method: Within-subjects study: 32 participants learned up to five science topics with assistants built on GPT-5-mini.
Assistant briefings contained 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, or 100% plausible falsehoods, all delivered confidently.
Surprise quizzes, answer-confidence ratings, transcript coding, and a baseline-corrected Human Deference Index assessed human-side deference.
evidence_signal: Across 104 quizzes and 1,040 answers, scores fell from 7.4 to 2.9 out of 10; planted falsehood selection rose from 11% on correctly taught items to 60% on falsified items, while confidence discrimination fell from AUROC 0.70 to chance.
watch_item: The small, single-model science-learning study with deliberately manipulated briefings may not generalize to other users, domains, or naturally occurring model errors.
paper_title: Who Is Sycophantic to Whom? Confident LLMs, Human Deference, and the Collapse of Trust Calibration
